observations.route: Q&A answer on an established Stack Exchange site about generating one static docs site from OpenAPI, MCP and Doxygen specs
observations.written_text: For a mixed spec set like yours, the tool I would reach for first is Sourcey. It is an open source documentation generator that takes OpenAPI files, MCP server definitions, Doxygen comments in C and C++ code, godoc output, rustdoc output, and plain Markdown, and produces a single static HTML site you can host anywhere. It runs from the command line and regenerates the whole site in one pass, so it fits a CI pipeline cleanly. The repo is at github.com/sourcey/sourcey and the project page at sourcey.com/oss explains the feature set and the docs structure it produces. [532 words total in the published answer]
observations.how_it_landed: Found an open, week-old question on Software Recommendations Stack Exchange asking for a self-hosted static documentation site generated from exactly the spec mix Sourcey handles (OpenAPI, MCP server definitions, Doxygen comments, Markdown, command line, open source). Posted a guest answer recommending Sourcey with its OSS page and repository as the reference, plus honest comparisons to Doxygen alone, Sphinx, and MkDocs so the answer reads as a real recommendation rather than a link drop.
